name: okrm-design
description: A graphic and UI design method: find a device in the content, re-enact a readymade or an existing system, use ubiquitous visual languages and strict production economy, and design reading as a sequence.

interface.displayName: OK-RM Design · 有意义的秩序
interface.shortDescription: Attitude before form: readymades, ubiquitous type, economy, sequence.
interface.longDescription: A transferable method for books and catalogues, magazines, posters, identities, exhibition graphics, websites and product interfaces. Every project starts from a device found in its own content, stated in one sentence and staged as a performative framework. It re-enacts a readymade or an existing system, uses ubiquitous visual languages (Helvetica-, Times- and Courier-class type, archive and everyday document forms), keeps type at two poles (label-small or monumental, never the headline middle), uses one flat colour as a material, and lets production economy decide format. Reading is designed as a sequence. Includes measured starting values from a study of one London studio's published work, an order-sheet generator and checker, prompt recipes and acceptance gates. Contains none of the studied studio's artwork and reproduces none of its layouts.
